historical_reviews.deepseek: Correctly separates physical handling from agent collection but omits power/ESD controls, exact slots, topology oracle and recovery proof.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly treats the case as a high-impact hybrid test rather than BLOCKED and prohibits software unbind/rescan substitution.
historical_reviews.history: Exact-code/source search found no earlier V3.1 record for this identity.
historical_reviews.v3_1: Fixed-BDF acceptance is not a simple set difference: disappearing endpoint functions are expected, while upstream bridge bus windows and every unaffected physical role must retain the approved domain:bus:device.function mapping across the controlled population change.

original_test_intent: Verify that removal of approved PCIe devices does not renumber reserved buses or alter the BDF/topology of unaffected devices.
original_method: Pin the exact hardware/firmware recipe and populated slot map, capture complete domain-qualified PCIe inventory and tree before service, have an authorized operator power-isolate and remove the approved devices under ESD controls, boot through the approved sequence, capture the reduced topology, compare reserved bus windows and unaffected physical-role BDFs, then reinsert and prove full recovery without software rescan/reset tricks.
manual_activity: An authorized operator performs the approved power isolation, PCIe device removal and reinsertion; a platform owner approves the expected reserved-bus and unaffected-topology oracle and decides the verdict.
safety_requirements: Drain workloads and use the approved shutdown/power-isolation procedure
Require ESD controls and authorized physical handling
Do not substitute driver unbind, hot-remove, rescan or reset
Stop on damage, unsafe state or boot failure
Preserve all inventories, photos and logs
Restore the full approved population before closure
agent_execution_scope: Collect complete read-only domain-qualified inventories and topology trees before, after and after recovery
Compare removed endpoints, reserved bus windows and unaffected topology
engineer_actions: Review boot, damage or BDF drift

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Two lspci captures are necessary but insufficient without domain-qualified topology, physical-role mapping, service safety and a recovery capture.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a read-only collector for complete domain-qualified inventory and topology before removal, after controlled boot with the approved devices absent, and after operator restoration; compare by physical role and reserved bus windows.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The fully populated/removed-device comparison and 40-minute activity remain; explicit service controls and recovery validation are added.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build three signed topology snapshots keyed by physical role—full population, approved reduced population and restored population—and compare expected disappearance separately from stable upstream bus windows and unaffected functions.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds an explicit slot oracle, safe physical lifecycle and recovery proof to the two informal lspci observations.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A flat device list can miss bridge-window renumbering or wrongly flag expected disappearance; physical-role/tree comparison distinguishes both.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Firmware resource allocation can depend on population and boot mode; the exact firmware settings and cold/warm boot sequence must be pinned for a meaningful result.

project_override_considerations: Define whether removal occurs only with AC isolated, the exact device subset and boot sequence, which bridges/bus windows remain reserved, how multifunction devices are counted, and the required restored-state topology.
expected_evidence: Approved service recipe, operator, ESD/power controls and device/slot photographs
Exact platform/firmware identity and populated slot map
Complete before/after/recovery domain-qualified inventory and topology with exit statuses
Physical-role comparison of removed functions, reserved bus windows and unaffected BDFs
Preserved system/PCIe logs and boot state
No-rescan/reset/unbind audit, recovery confirmation and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently define a physical population change and fixed-BDF comparison. The unspecified removal safety and comparison granularity are material omissions, not contradictory objectives.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The test is executable as a governed operator-agent workflow. It becomes BLOCKED if safe physical access, the fixed-BDF oracle, exact slot map or recovery path is unavailable.

review_improvement: Turns an unsafe two-list comparison into a controlled three-state topology experiment with physical-role and recovery evidence.
independent_technical_reasoning: Removing an endpoint legitimately removes its functions, but fixed-BDF firmware is expected to preserve the resource windows that keep unaffected roles stable. Comparison must therefore separate endpoint absence from bridge-window allocation and map surviving BDFs to the same physical roles; raw line-by-line lspci equality would encode the wrong oracle.
